Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Weather Newsletters 'French protests become violent' and SAS men 'arrested for murder' 1 day ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Some editions of the Sunday Telegraph picture the historic clock tower in the French city of Limoges collapsing in flames , as protests raged across the country. The paper says crowds were "heard cheering" as the tower fell. "War de France" is the Sun on Sunday's headline. It says President Emmanuel Macron has been "blasted" after he was pictured dancing with his wife in a private box at a Celine Dion concert the previous night.
The Sunday Times says five SAS soldiers were sent back to the battlefield just 48 hours after they were questioned by military police on suspicion of murdering two people in Syria in 2022. It later emerged those killed were teenagers working for the Islamic State group. The paper says the men were "left in limbo" for three years before being told no charges would be brought. The Ministry of Defence says its soldiers are "entitled to expect any investigation is conducted fairly and professionally."
The Mail on Sunday - on its front page - says the BBC has been accused of "brainwashing" children who use its educational website, Bitesize . The paper reports that the site encourages users to play an online game called "Increasing Immigration", in which players get extra points if they choose options such as "open borders". The BBC says players are not rewarded for choosing political positions, but it will review the examples highlighted in the story.
The Observer says a "national emergency" of childhood has been declared by the children's commissioner for England. Rachel de Souza tells the paper the lives of too many children were "Dickensian with a modern twist". She'll release what's been described as a "damning report" tomorrow. It apparently exposes "vast inequalities" across England - such as children in Blackpool being 27 times more likely to miss school than pupils in Lambeth.
The Sunday Express leads on Nigel Farage's warning to Andy Burnham that Britain will never "vote to rejoin" the European Union . The Reform UK leader says people in Labour's traditional heartlands will prevent the Prime Minister from leading Britain back into the bloc. A No 10 spokesperson tells the paper that the government had inherited a "threadbare Brexit deal" and that it was working on agreements that "pay pff for British farmers and families".
The Mail on Sunday looks ahead to tonight's edition of The Archers on Radio 4 , which will feature the drama's first "lesbian wedding". The paper says "six million fans" are expected to tune in, with BBC insiders predicting a high number of younger listeners. The paper notes the show has kept pace with the times, having tackled "everything from steamy affairs... to modern slavery and even coercive control".
